subproblems.title: A Borel countably n-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces
subproblems.statement: Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.bilipschitz_pieces-a1, accepted candidate commit a2ba78f), whose frozen Lean type is reused verbatim; no new formal work is needed. It is used by the sibling refined_pieces (step 1) and carries out step 2 of the parent proof (parametrization of M₁ by disjoint bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces with injective derivatives). Its audited proof is reproduced below; in that text, "the parent proof" and "sibling" refer to the decomposition of root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1, in which it was proved, not to the present node.
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (with the n = 0 provisions of its step 10). It plays the role of Simon's decomposition of Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75: M = ⋃_j M_j disjoint, M_j ⊆ N_j, H^n(M_0) = 0), with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds; families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, the lower bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability/injectivity of DF_i hold on B_i, and F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then P_{i'} ⊆ N_{i'} and P_i ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the P_i are pairwise disjoint. (This is the parent's recursive definition B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})) in closed form: by induction ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = M ∩ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}.)
8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. Then a ∈ t_{j,k} for some k, so a ∈ D_i for the index i with (j(i), k(i)) = (j, k), and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i₀ is the least index with x ∈ N_{i₀}, then x ∈ P_{i₀}. Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), so H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. n = 0 and n > P need no separate treatment: for n = 0 every A is injective, m(A) = 1, r(A) = 1/2, every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative (G_j = ℝ^0), and each D_i ⊆ ℝ^0 has at most one point; for n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, so all G_j are empty, all B_i = ∅, and step 8 says H^n(M) = 0. (Imports: areaRegularSet and its lemmas live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the frozen statement does not use it.)
proof_key_steps: Cover M by M₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) and remove the null images F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) of the non-regular points.
Radius r(A) := m(A)/2 for injective A (m(A) a coercivity constant, 1 when n = 0), r(A) := 1 otherwise, so r(A) ≠ 0 for all A.
Mathlib's partition theorem gives pieces G_j ∩ t_{j,k} on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant r(A_{j,k}).
Enumerate the pieces over ℕ; their images are Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(D_{i'})) yields disjoint Borel images in M covering M up to a null set.

Source: step 5 of the parent proof (density lemma). 7. Dimension zero. The argument is valid for n = 0 as written: ℝ^0 = {0}, λ is the unit point mass, B ⊆ {0}, ω_0 = 1 and r^{±0} = 1, J_F ≡ 1 (normDet of a map out of ℝ^0, LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton), (γ) is vacuous, D = {0}, integrals over ℝ^0 are evaluations at 0, and range L_b = {0} has finrank 0. subproblems.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ and f : ℝ^m → ℝ^P. Let Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (the zero map where f is not differentiable), e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, and Jf(x) := (det[⟨Df(x)e_k, Df(x)e_l⟩]_{k,l})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). Then (i) Jf : ℝ^m → ℝ is Borel measurable; (ii) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^m such that f is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective and f is injective on s, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and λ := volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m.

subproblems.title: An integer-valued density on an oriented rectifiable set gives an IMRep

2. (Multiplicity.) mult(x) := ⌊|m(x)|⌋₊ ∈ ℕ (Nat.floor). For every x, m(x) = z for some z ∈ ℤ, and |m(x)| = |z| is the natural number natAbs z, so (mult(x) : ℝ) = |m(x)|. mult is measurable as the composition of the measurable m, the continuous |·| and the monotone, hence measurable, ⌊·⌋₊ : ℝ → ℕ (Monotone.measurable). For x ∈ N', m(x) ≠ 0, so mult(x) = |m(x)| > 0.
3. (Orientation.) orient(x) := −η(x) if m(x) < 0, and orient(x) := η(x) otherwise. It is strongly measurable: η and −η = (−1)•η are strongly measurable, {m < 0} is Borel, and the piecewise combination is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.ite). In particular orient is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞N'.
4. (Rectifiability, local integrability.) N' ⊆ N, so N' is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono). For compact K ⊆ U: ∫_{N'∩K} mult dμ ≤ ∫_{N∩K} mult dμ = ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ < ∞, by monotonicity in the set, step 2 and the hypothesis.
5. (Orientation field.) Apply sibling tangent_locality with open U, small set N' and large set N. Here N' ⊆ N ⊆ U are Borel and N is locally finite by hypothesis. So for μ⌞N'-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q. The hypothesis on η holds μ⌞N-a.e., hence μ⌞N'-a.e., since N' ⊆ N. Take x outside both exceptional null sets and Q from the hypothesis. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q, and orient(x) ∈ {η(x), −η(x)} is a unit orientation of Q. Indeed, if η(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α (resp. −α(τ)), with τ orthonormal spanning Q, then −η(x)(α) = −α(τ) (resp. α(τ)); IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign with the same τ.
6. Steps 1–5 verify every field of IMRep (measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, locallyIntegrable_mult, aestronglyMeasurable_orient, orients). So R := (N', mult, orient) is an IMRep in U.
7. (Action.) Let ω be any n-form. For x ∈ N:
   - if m(x) = 0, then x ∉ N' and 1_{N'}(x)·mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = 0 = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x));
   - if m(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ N' and mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = |m(x)|·(±η(x)(ω(x))) = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)), the sign being that of m(x).
   So the functions 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) and m·η(ω) agree at every point of N. Hence R.action(ω) = ∫_{N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ = ∫_{N ∩ N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ (since N ∩ N' = N') = ∫_N 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) dμ (setIntegral_indicator) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dμ (setIntegral_congr_fun). No integrability is needed: Bochner integrals over N of functions that agree pointwise on N coincide. ∎

subproblems.title: C¹ cut-off: a globally C¹, Lipschitz map agreeing with f to first order on K
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^P open, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact with K ⊆ O, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on O (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O). Then there are φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P of class C¹ on all of ℝ^P (ContDiff ℝ 1 φ) and Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 such that φ is Λ-Lipschitz and, for every x ∈ K, φ(x) = f(x) and Dφ(x) = Df(x) (D = fderiv ℝ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (O K : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsOpen O → IsCompact K → K ⊆ O → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 f O → ∃ (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ ∧ LipschitzWith Λ φ ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, φ x = f x ∧ fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1(b) of the parent proof (cut-off of f), carried out in full.
1. Margin. By IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open (K compact, O open, K ⊆ O) there is ε > 0 with cthickening ε K ⊆ O. Put δ := ε/3 > 0, W₀ := thickening δ K (open), W₁ := cthickening δ K (closed) and V := thickening (2δ) K (open). Then K ⊆ W₀ ⊆ W₁ ⊆ V (Metric.self_subset_thickening for δ > 0, thickening_subset_cthickening, and cthickening δ K ⊆ thickening (2δ) K since δ < 2δ), and closure V ⊆ cthickening (2δ) K ⊆ cthickening ε K ⊆ O. The set cthickening (2δ) K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening; ℝ^P is proper), so closure V is a compact subset of O. (If K = ∅ all these sets are empty and the construction below gives φ = id.)
2. Smooth cut-off. By exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (V open, W₁ closed, W₁ ⊆ V) there is χ : ℝ^P → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ ⊤ χ (in particular C¹), range χ ⊆ [0, 1], support χ = V and χ(x) = 1 ⟺ x ∈ W₁. Hence tsupport χ = closure V is compact and contained in O, and χ = 1 on the open set W₀ ⊇ K.
3. Definition. φ(x) := x + χ(x)·(f(x) − x).
4. φ is C¹. Let x ∈ ℝ^P. If x ∈ O, then f is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn on the open set O gives ContDiffAt ℝ 1 f x), so x ↦ x + χ(x)(f(x) − x) is ContDiffAt ℝ 1 at x (sums and products of C¹ functions). If x ∉ tsupport χ, the open set (tsupport χ)ᶜ is a neighbourhood of x on which χ = 0, so φ = id near x and φ is ContDiffAt ℝ 1 at x (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). As tsupport χ ⊆ O, every x falls under one of the two cases, so ContDiff ℝ 1 φ (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).
5. First-order agreement on K. For x ∈ K, W₀ is an open neighbourhood of x on which χ = 1, i.e. φ = f on W₀. Hence φ(x) = f(x) and φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f, so fderiv ℝ φ x = fderiv ℝ f x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
6. Lipschitz bound. Dφ is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, order 1 ≠ 0), so ‖Dφ‖ ≤ C on the compact set tsupport χ for some C ≥ 0 (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). For x ∉ tsupport χ, φ = id near x, so Dφ(x) = id and ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ 1. Thus ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ := max(1, C) (as an element of ℝ≥0) for every x. φ is differentiable on the convex set ℝ^P, so the mean value inequality lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_fderiv_le gives that φ is Λ-Lipschitz.
7. Steps 4–6 give ContDiff ℝ 1 φ, LipschitzWith Λ φ and φ(x) = f(x), Dφ(x) = Df(x) for x ∈ K. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening(3δ, K) ⊆ O and a smooth χ ∈ [0,1] equal to 1 exactly on cthickening(δ, K) with support thickening(2δ, K).
φ := id + χ·(f − id) is C¹: near points of O because f is C¹ there, near points off tsupport χ because φ = id there.
φ = f on the open set thickening(δ, K) ⊇ K, so φ and Dφ agree with f and Df on K.
Dφ is continuous and equal to id off the compact tsupport χ, hence bounded by Λ; the mean value inequality makes φ Λ-Lipschitz.

subproblems.title: Algebra of unit orientations: sign uniqueness, the bound |ξ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖, and the normalized orientation A_#e/J_A of range A
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ: (a) if ξ and ξ' are unit orientations of the same linear subspace T ⊆ ℝ^P (IsUnitOrientationOf), then ξ' = ξ or ξ' = −ξ; (b) if ξ is a unit orientation of some subspace, then |ξ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every n-covector β (operator norm); (c) if A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is an injective continuous linear map, e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1 and J_A := (det[⟨Ae_k, Ae_l⟩]_{k,l})^{1/2}, then J_A > 0 and the n-vector J_A⁻¹·A_#e, i.e. β ↦ J_A⁻¹·β(Ae_1, …, Ae_n), is a unit orientation of range A; (d) if A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is a continuous linear map that is not injective, then β(Ae_1, …, Ae_n) = 0 for every n-covector β.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: (A0) (last clause), (A1) and (A2) of the parent proof. Notation: for an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P, IsUnitOrientationOf ξ (span τ) is witnessed by τ when ξ(α) = α(τ) for all α or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for all α.
1. Expansion lemma (E). Let τ be orthonormal in ℝ^P, V := span τ, and b_1, …, b_n ∈ V. Then α(b) = det(M)·α(τ) for every n-covector α, where M_ij := ⟨τ_i, b_j⟩. Proof: τ is linearly independent (orthonormal), hence a basis of V, and its coordinate functionals are v ↦ ⟨τ_i, v⟩, so b_j = Σ_i M_ij τ_i. The restriction α_V of α to V^n (α composed with the inclusion V ↪ ℝ^P) is an alternating n-linear form on V; by AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, α_V = α_V(τ)·det_τ, and det_τ(b) is the determinant of the coordinate matrix of b in the basis τ, which is M (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). Hence α(b) = det(M)·α(τ).
2. Parseval (G). With τ, V as in step 1 and b, b' ∈ V: ⟨b, b'⟩ = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, b⟩⟨τ_i, b'⟩ (expand b' = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, b'⟩τ_i and use linearity of the inner product). Hence for b_1, …, b_n ∈ V the Gram matrix (⟨b_k, b_l⟩)_{k,l} equals MᵀM with M as in step 1, and det(⟨b_k, b_l⟩) = det(M)².
3. Proof of (b). Let τ witness IsUnitOrientationOf ξ T. Then ξ(β) = ±β(τ) and |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_i‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; ‖τ_i‖ = 1). So |ξ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖.
4. Proof of (a). Let τ, τ' witness the two hypotheses: ξ(α) = s·α(τ), ξ'(α) = s'·α(τ') for all α, with s, s' ∈ {1, −1} and span τ = T = span τ'. Each τ'_j lies in span τ, so by (E) α(τ') = det(O)·α(τ) for every α, where O_ij := ⟨τ_i, τ'_j⟩. By (G) applied to b := τ', (OᵀO)_jk = ⟨τ'_j, τ'_k⟩ = δ_jk, so det(O)² = det(OᵀO) = 1 and det O ∈ {1, −1}. Therefore ξ'(α) = s'·det(O)·α(τ) = (s'·det(O)·s)·ξ(α) for every α (s² = 1), with c := s'·det(O)·s ∈ {1, −1}: ξ' = ξ if c = 1 and ξ' = −ξ if c = −1 (ext on covectors).
5. Proof of (d). If A is not injective there is v ≠ 0 with Av = 0; writing v = Σ_k v_k e_k (e is a basis) gives Σ_k v_k·Ae_k = 0 with some v_k ≠ 0, so the family (Ae_1, …, Ae_n) is linearly dependent, and every alternating multilinear map vanishes on a linearly dependent family (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent applied to β viewed as an alternating map). So β(Ae) = 0.
6. Proof of (c). Let A be injective and V := range A. Since A is injective, finrank V = finrank ℝⁿ = n; choose an orthonormal basis of V indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V reindexed along finrank V = n) and let τ_i ∈ ℝ^P be its vectors. Then τ is orthonormal, span τ = V, and b_j := Ae_j ∈ V. Put M_ij := ⟨τ_i, Ae_j⟩. (i) M is invertible: if Mc = 0 for some c ∈ ℝⁿ, then A(Σ_j c_j e_j) = Σ_j c_j Ae_j = Σ_i (Mc)_i τ_i = 0, so Σ_j c_j e_j = 0 and c = 0. (ii) By (G), det(⟨Ae_k, Ae_l⟩) = det(M)² > 0, hence J_A = (det(M)²)^{1/2} = |det M| > 0. (iii) By (E), β(Ae) = det(M)·β(τ) for every β, so J_A⁻¹·β(Ae) = (det M/|det M|)·β(τ) = s·β(τ) with s := sign(det M) ∈ {1, −1} independent of β. Hence the n-vector J_A⁻¹·A_#e is a unit orientation of range A, witnessed by τ (span τ = range A) and the sign s. For n = 0 everything is consistent: Fin 0 matrices have determinant 1, J_A = 1, V = ⊥ and τ is empty. ∎

Source: (A3) of the parent proof, the Lusin–Souslin and null-set transfer facts of its step 2, and the "injective area formula ... applied to the positive and negative parts" of its steps 3, 6 and 8, isolated as one toolkit. Siblings used: gram_area (accepted codim1_lura_gram_area_formula) and orient_algebra (only its clause (c), J_T > 0 for injective T). Lⁿ := volume on ℝⁿ.
1. Linear area identity. Let T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be an injective continuous linear map and S ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel. T is differentiable everywhere with DT(x) = T (ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv), injective, and injective on S; gram_area (m := n, f := T, s := S, g := 1) gives Hⁿ(T(S)) = ∫⁻_S ofReal(J_T) dx = ofReal(J_T)·Lⁿ(S).
2. Proof of (I). If L∘A is injective, so is A. Let S := ball(0, 1) ⊆ ℝⁿ; 0 < Lⁿ(S) < ∞ (also for n = 0, where S = {0} has measure 1). By step 1, Hⁿ((L∘A)(S)) = ofReal(J_{L∘A})·Lⁿ(S) and Hⁿ(A(S)) = ofReal(J_A)·Lⁿ(S). The linear map L is ‖L‖-Lipschitz, so LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le gives μH[n](L(X)) ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·μH[n](X) for every X; μHE[n] is a fixed positive multiple of μH[n] (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), so the same holds for Hⁿ. With X := A(S) and (L∘A)(S) = L(A(S)): ofReal(J_{L∘A})·Lⁿ(S) ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·ofReal(J_A)·Lⁿ(S). Dividing by Lⁿ(S) ∈ (0, ∞) and using J ≥ 0 gives J_{L∘A} ≤ ‖L‖ⁿ·J_A.
3. (i) F is differentiable, hence continuous, at every point of B, so ContinuousOn F B. As B is Borel, F is injective on B and ℝⁿ is Polish, F(B) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
4. (ii) Let c be the point of ℝⁿ that Function.invFunOn returns when y has no preimage in B. For y ∈ F(B), ψ(y) ∈ B and F(ψ(y)) = y, and ψ(y) is the unique such point (injectivity); for y ∉ F(B), ψ(y) = c. Hence for Borel S ⊆ ℝⁿ: ψ⁻¹(S) = F(B ∩ S) ∪ (F(B)ᶜ if c ∈ S, ∅ otherwise). F(B ∩ S) is Borel by step 3 applied to the Borel set B ∩ S ⊆ B, and F(B) is Borel, so ψ is measurable.
5. Area formula. gram_area (m := n, f := F, s := B) gives: x ↦ J(x) is Borel, and (AF) ∫⁻_{F(B)} g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(x))·g(F(x)) dx for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. By orient_algebra (c) applied to the injective DF(x), J(x) > 0 for every x ∈ B.
6. (iii) Let p hold for Hⁿ⌞F(B)-a.e. y. Choose a Borel set Z with (Hⁿ⌞F(B))(Z) = Hⁿ(Z ∩ F(B)) = 0 such that p(y) holds for every y ∉ Z (exists_measurable_superset_of_null). By (AF) with g := 1_Z, ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(x))·1_Z(F(x)) dx = Hⁿ(Z ∩ F(B)) = 0. The integrand is a.e.-measurable on B (J Borel; F a.e.-measurable on B by ContinuousOn.aemeasurable), so it vanishes for a.e. x ∈ B (lintegral_eq_zero_iff'), and since J(x) > 0 on B, F(x) ∉ Z, hence p(F(x)), for a.e. x ∈ B.
7. Measurability. Let h be a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞F(B) and h̃ strongly measurable with h = h̃ Hⁿ⌞F(B)-a.e. By (iii), h(F(x)) = h̃(F(x)) for a.e. x ∈ B. x ↦ h̃(F(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on B (AEStronglyMeasurable.comp_aemeasurable with the a.e.-measurable F), so x ↦ J(x)·h(F(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable on B.
8. Integrability. (AF) with g := ‖h‖ₑ gives ∫⁻_{F(B)} ‖h‖ₑ dHⁿ = ∫⁻_B ofReal(J(x))·‖h(F(x))‖ₑ dx = ∫⁻_B ‖J(x)·h(F(x))‖ₑ dx (J ≥ 0). With step 7 and the hypothesis, IntegrableOn h F(B) ⟺ IntegrableOn (J·h∘F) B.
9. Equality. If h is integrable on F(B): ∫_{F(B)} h = ∫⁻_{F(B)} ofReal(h) − ∫⁻_{F(B)} ofReal(−h) (integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part); by (AF) with g := ofReal∘h and g := ofReal∘(−h) and ofReal(J)·ofReal(t) = ofReal(J·t) for J ≥ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_mul), these equal ∫⁻_B ofReal(J·h∘F) and ∫⁻_B ofReal(−J·h∘F), whose difference is ∫_B J·h∘F (same lemma; J·h∘F is integrable by step 8). If h is not integrable on F(B), then J·h∘F is not integrable on B (step 8), and both Bochner integrals are 0 by definition. So ∫_{F(B)} h dHⁿ = ∫_B J(x)h(F(x)) dx in all cases. ∎

Source: steps 2 and 7 of the parent proof (parametrization of M₁, then the split of each piece into the critical part {DH_i not injective} and bi-Lipschitz pieces of H_i = φ∘G_i "exactly as in step 2(iv)"), done once for all pieces. Sibling used: bilipschitz_pieces (accepted dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces).
1. Parametrization. bilipschitz_pieces applied to M gives Lipschitz F_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Borel B_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) with m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| on B_i, F_i differentiable with injective derivative on B_i, F_i(B_i) Borel ⊆ M, pairwise disjoint, and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0. In particular F_i is injective on B_i.
2. Critical and regular parts. Put H_i := φ∘F_i. For a ∈ B_i, H_i is differentiable at a with DH_i(a) = Dφ(F_i(a))∘DF_i(a) (chain rule; φ is differentiable everywhere). Let C_i := {a ∈ B_i : DH_i(a) is not injective} and B_i⁺ := B_i ∖ C_i. C_i is Borel: a ↦ DH_i(a) = fderiv ℝ H_i a is Borel (measurable_fderiv), and the set of injective continuous linear maps ℝⁿ → ℝ^P is open — if L is injective there is c > 0 with |Lv| ≥ c|v| for all v (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith), and then |L'v| ≥ (c/2)|v| whenever ‖L' − L‖ < c/2 — hence Borel (IsOpen.measurableSet). So C_i and B_i⁺ are Borel.
3. Coercivity radius. For injective continuous linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P choose c_A > 0 with |Av| ≥ c_A|v| for all v (as in step 2), and define r : (ℝⁿ →L[ℝ] ℝ^P) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := c_A/2 for injective A and r(A) := 1 otherwise; then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Bi-Lipschitz pieces of H_i. If B_i⁺ = ∅, put t_{i,l} := ∅ and κ_{i,l} := 1 for all l. Otherwise, for a ∈ B_i⁺, HasFDerivWithinAt H_i (DH_i(a)) B_i⁺ a, and Mathlib's exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f := H_i, s := B_i⁺, f' := fderiv ℝ H_i, radius r) gives pairwise disjoint measurable t_{i,l} (l ∈ ℕ) with B_i⁺ ⊆ ⋃_l t_{i,l} and continuous linear A_{i,l} with |H_i(a) − H_i(a') − A_{i,l}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{i,l})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ B_i⁺ ∩ t_{i,l}, where each A_{i,l} = DH_i(y) for some y ∈ B_i⁺, hence injective with r(A_{i,l}) = c/2, c := c_{A_{i,l}}. Then |H_i(a) − H_i(a')| ≥ c|a − a'| − (c/2)|a − a'| = (c/2)|a − a'| on B_i⁺ ∩ t_{i,l}; put κ_{i,l} := c/2 > 0.
5. Enumeration. For i, k ∈ ℕ put A_{i,0} := C_i, A_{i,l+1} := B_i⁺ ∩ t_{i,l}, G_{i,k} := F_i and κ_{i,k} := m_i. Enumerate ℕ × ℕ by j ↦ (i, k) := Nat.unpair j and set G_j := G_{i,k}, A_j := A_{i,k}, κ_j := κ_{i,k}.
6. Properties inherited from step 1. G_j = F_i is Lipschitz; A_j is Borel; κ_j = m_i > 0; since A_j ⊆ B_i, the bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability with injective derivative hold on A_j; G_j(A_j) is Borel (F_i is continuous and injective on the Borel set A_j, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn); G_j(A_j) ⊆ F_i(B_i) ⊆ M.
7. Disjointness. Let j ≠ j' correspond to (i, k) ≠ (i', k'). If i ≠ i', G_j(A_j) ⊆ F_i(B_i) and G_{j'}(A_{j'}) ⊆ F_{i'}(B_{i'}) are disjoint. If i = i', then k ≠ k' and A_{i,k} ∩ A_{i,k'} = ∅ (C_i ∩ B_i⁺ = ∅ and the t_{i,l} are pairwise disjoint); F_i is injective on B_i ⊇ A_{i,k} ∪ A_{i,k'}, so the images are disjoint.
8. Null remainder. ⋃_k A_{i,k} = C_i ∪ (B_i⁺ ∩ ⋃_l t_{i,l}) = C_i ∪ B_i⁺ = B_i, so ⋃_j G_j(A_j) = ⋃_i F_i(B_i) (Nat.unpair is a bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ) and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j G_j(A_j)) = Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. Dichotomy. If k = 0: for every a ∈ A_j = C_i, D(φ∘G_j)(a) = DH_i(a) is not injective (critical). If k = l + 1: κ' := κ_{i,l} > 0 satisfies κ'|a − a'| ≤ |φ(G_j(a)) − φ(G_j(a'))| for a, a' ∈ A_j = B_i⁺ ∩ t_{i,l} (step 4), and D(φ∘G_j)(a) = DH_i(a) is injective for a ∈ B_i⁺ (regular). ∎

Split B_i into the Borel critical set C_i = {D(φ∘F_i) not injective} and B_i⁺ = B_i ∖ C_i (fderiv is Borel; injective maps form an open set).
Mathlib's partition theorem with radius c_A/2 cuts B_i⁺ into Borel pieces on which φ∘F_i is bi-Lipschitz.
Enumerate the pieces (i,0) ↦ C_i, (i,l+1) ↦ B_i⁺ ∩ t_{i,l} by Nat.unpair; images stay Borel, disjoint, inside M and cover M up to the same null set.

By (a): LHS(β) := ∫_{G(A)} h_β dHⁿ = ∫_A J_G(a)·θ(G(a))·ξ(G(a))(β(H(a))∘Dφ(G(a))) da.
 (c) J_G(a) > 0 for a ∈ A, by orient_algebra (c) applied to the injective DG(a).
 (d) Let ξ̃ be strongly measurable with ξ̃ = ξ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.mk); then ξ̃ = ξ Hⁿ⌞G(A)-a.e. (G(A) ⊆ M), so by (a) ξ̃(G(a)) = ξ(G(a)) for a.e. a ∈ A.
 (e) By (★) and the chain rule, for a.e. a ∈ A there is σ_a ∈ {1, −1} with, for every covector α, J_G(a)·ξ(G(a))(α∘Dφ(G(a))) = σ_a·(α∘Dφ(G(a)))(DG(a)e) = σ_a·α(DH(a)e_1, …, DH(a)e_n).
2. Critical case (D(φ∘G)(a) not injective for every a ∈ A). Take N := ∅, g := 0, η := 0. Then N is Borel, N ⊆ φ(G(A)), N is countably n-rectifiable (Hⁿ(∅) = 0), g is measurable, η is strongly measurable, the a.e. statement over Hⁿ⌞∅ = 0 is trivial, and ∫⁻_∅ |g| = 0 ≤ Λⁿ∫⁻_{G(A)} θ. For the identity: by orient_algebra (d) applied to DH(a), α(DH(a)e) = 0 for every α and a ∈ A, so by (e) the integrand in 1(b) vanishes for a.e. a ∈ A and LHS(β) = 0 = ∫_∅ g·η(β) dHⁿ.
3. Regular case (κ' > 0 with κ'|a − a'| ≤ |H(a) − H(a')| on A, DH(a) injective for a ∈ A).

Put N := H(A) ⊆ φ(G(A)). change_of_variables (II) for (F, B) := (H, A) gives: N is Borel, ψ := invFunOn H A is measurable, and ∫_N h dHⁿ = ∫_A J_H(a)h(H(a)) da for every h a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N. N ⊆ range H with H Lipschitz, so N is countably n-rectifiable (definition with M₀ := ∅ and the constant sequence H, or Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_range and CountablyRectifiable.mono).
 (b) Definitions. g(y) := θ(G(ψ(y))) (as an integer) for y ∈ N and g(y) := 0 for y ∉ N. η(y) := (J_G(ψ(y))/J_H(ψ(y)))·(ξ̃(G(ψ(y)))∘C(y)), where C(y) := compContinuousLinearMapCLM(Dφ(G(ψ(y)))), i.e. η(y)(α) = (J_G(ψ y)/J_H(ψ y))·ξ̃(G(ψ y))(α∘Dφ(G(ψ y))). g is measurable (θ measurable, G continuous, ψ measurable, N Borel). η is strongly measurable: J_G, J_H are Borel (gram_area (i)), so c(y) := J_G(ψ y)/J_H(ψ y) is measurable; ξ̃∘G∘ψ is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.comp_measurable); y ↦ C(y) is strongly measurable (ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM.comp_stronglyMeasurable applied to (measurable_fderiv ℝ φ).stronglyMeasurable, composed with the measurable G∘ψ); and y ↦ c(y)•(ξ̃(G(ψ y))).comp(C(y)) is strongly measurable by hc.stronglyMeasurable.smul ((continuous_fst.clm_comp continuous_snd).comp_stronglyMeasurable (hξ.prodMk hC)). For y ∈ N, G(ψ(y)) ∈ G(A) ⊆ M, so θ(G(ψ y)) > 0 (R.mult_pos) and g(y) ≠ 0.
 (c) Jacobian comparison (parent (A3)): for a ∈ A, DH(a) = Dφ(G(a))∘DG(a) is injective, so change_of_variables (I) with (A, L) := (DG(a), Dφ(G(a))) gives J_H(a) ≤ ‖Dφ(G(a))‖ⁿ·J_G(a) ≤ Λⁿ·J_G(a).
 (d) Mass bound. By gram_area for (H, A) with g := |g|, the identities g(H(a)) = θ(G(a)) (a ∈ A), step (c), and gram_area for (G, A) with g := θ: ∫⁻_N |g| dHⁿ = ∫⁻_A ofReal(J_H(a))·θ(G(a)) da ≤ Λⁿ·∫⁻_A ofReal(J_G(a))·θ(G(a)) da = Λⁿ·∫⁻_{G(A)} θ dHⁿ. In particular Hⁿ(N) ≤ ∫⁻_N |g| < ∞ (|g| ≥ 1 on N).
 (e) Orientation. piece_tangent with (U := ℝ^P, Y := N, F := H, B := A, L := ΛL, m := κ') (N Borel, Hⁿ(N ∩ C) ≤ Hⁿ(N) < ∞, H(A) = N) gives: for a.e. a ∈ A, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N (H(a)) (range DH(a)). Let A₀ ⊆ A be a Borel Lⁿ-null set outside which this, 1(d) and 1(e) hold. gram_area on A₀ gives Hⁿ(H(A₀)) = ∫⁻_{A₀} ofReal(J_H) = 0. Let y ∈ N ∖ H(A₀) and a := ψ(y) ∈ A ∖ A₀, so H(a) = y. By 1(d), 1(e): η(y)(α) = J_H(a)⁻¹·J_G(a)·ξ(G(a))(α∘Dφ(G(a))) = σ_a·J_H(a)⁻¹·α(DH(a)e) for every α. By orient_algebra (c) for the injective DH(a), J_H(a)⁻¹·DH(a)_#e is a unit orientation of range DH(a); its negative is one as well (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign with the same orthonormal frame). So η(y) is a unit orientation of range DH(a), which is an approximate tangent space of N at y. This holds for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N.
 (f) Identity. Let β be strongly measurable; y ↦ g(y)·η(y)(β(y)) is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N. By 3(a), ∫_N g·η(β) dHⁿ = ∫_A J_H(a)·g(H(a))·η(H(a))(β(H(a))) da = ∫_A J_H(a)·θ(G(a))·(J_G(a)/J_H(a))·ξ̃(G(a))(β(H(a))∘Dφ(G(a))) da. As J_H(a) > 0 on A (orient_algebra (c) for the injective DH(a)) and ξ̃(G(a)) = ξ(G(a)) for a.e. a ∈ A (1(d)), the integrand equals J_G(a)·θ(G(a))·ξ(G(a))(β(H(a))∘Dφ(G(a))) for a.e. a ∈ A, so ∫_N g·η(β) dHⁿ = LHS(β) by 1(b).
4. Steps 2 and 3 give N, g, η with all the stated properties in both cases. ∎

subproblems.title: An integer-valued measurable density from a summable family of integer functions
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and f_j : ℝ^P → ℤ measurable (j ∈ ℕ) with Σ_j ∫⁻ |f_j| dHⁿ < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then there is a measurable m : ℝ^P → ℝ with m(y) ∈ ℤ for every y, |m(y)| ≤ Σ_j |f_j(y)| (in [0, ∞]) for every y, and, for Hⁿ-a.e. y, the real family (f_j(y))_j is summable and m(y) = Σ_j f_j(y).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (f : ℕ → Euclid P → ℤ), (∀ j, Measurable (f j)) → ∑' j, ∫⁻ y, ((f j y).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] ≠ ∞ → ∃ m : Euclid P → ℝ, Measurable m ∧ (∀ y, ∃ z : ℤ, m y = z) ∧ (∀ y, ENNReal.ofReal |m y| ≤ ∑' j, ((f j y).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞)) ∧ ∀ᵐ y ∂μHE[n], Summable (fun j => (f j y : ℝ)) ∧ m y = ∑' j, (f j y : ℝ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 10 of the parent proof ("k agrees Hⁿ-a.e. with a Borel ℤ-valued function k̃"), in the form needed by the sibling imrep_of_density (measurable and integer valued at every point).
1. Notation. S(y) := Σ'_j |f_j(y)| ∈ [0, ∞] (ℝ≥0∞-valued tsum of the measurable functions y ↦ ((f_j y).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞)); S is measurable (Measurable.ennreal_tsum, or its current name Measurable.tsum). For y and j put p_j(y) := (max(f_j(y), 0) : ℝ≥0) and q_j(y) := (max(−f_j(y), 0) : ℝ≥0) (Real.toNNReal of ±f_j(y)); both are measurable, take values in ℕ ⊆ ℝ≥0, and p_j(y) − q_j(y) = f_j(y), p_j(y) + q_j(y) = |f_j(y)|.
2. Definition. m(y) := (Σ'_j p_j(y) : ℝ≥0) − (Σ'_j q_j(y) : ℝ≥0), the tsums taken in ℝ≥0 (equal to 0 when the family is not summable) and cast to ℝ. m is measurable (Measurable.nnreal_tsum — a deprecated alias that still works; Measurable.tsum is the current name — for each tsum, then coercion and subtraction).
3. Integrality. Let (a_j) be a family in ℝ≥0 with every a_j a natural number. If (a_j) is summable, a_j → 0 along the cofinite filter (Summable.tendsto_cofinite_zero), so the set F := {j : a_j ≥ 1} is finite and a_j = 0 for j ∉ F (a natural number < 1 is 0); hence Σ' a_j = Σ_{j∈F} a_j (tsum_eq_sum) is a natural number. If (a_j) is not summable, Σ' a_j = 0 (tsum_eq_zero_of_not_summable). Applied to (p_j(y)) and (q_j(y)), m(y) is a difference of two natural numbers, an integer.
4. Pointwise bound. If S(y) = ∞ there is nothing to prove. If S(y) < ∞, then Σ'_j (p_j(y) + q_j(y) : ℝ≥0∞) = S(y) < ∞, so both families (p_j(y)) and (q_j(y)) are summable in ℝ≥0 (ENNReal.tsum_coe_ne_top_iff_summable and comparison) and |m(y)| ≤ Σ'_j p_j(y) + Σ'_j q_j(y) = S(y).
5. Almost everywhere. ∫⁻ S dHⁿ = Σ_j ∫⁻ |f_j| dHⁿ < ∞ (lintegral_tsum; each term is measurable), so S(y) < ∞ for Hⁿ-a.e. y (ae_lt_top). For such y, Σ_j |f_j(y)| < ∞, so the real family (f_j(y)) is summable (absolutely summable real families are summable), (p_j(y)) and (q_j(y)) are summable (step 4), and Σ'_j f_j(y) = Σ'_j p_j(y) − Σ'_j q_j(y) = m(y) (Summable.tsum_sub for summable families, and NNReal.coe_tsum).
6. Steps 2–5 give m. ∎
proof_key_steps: S := Σ_j|f_j| is measurable with ∫⁻S = Σ_j∫⁻|f_j| < ∞, so S < ∞ a.e.
m := Σ_j f_j⁺ − Σ_j f_j⁻ with ℝ≥0-valued tsums is measurable (Measurable.nnreal_tsum).
A summable family of natural numbers has finite support, so each tsum is a natural number (or 0 if not summable): m is integer valued everywhere.
|m| ≤ S pointwise, and m = Σ_j f_j wherever S < ∞, i.e. a.e.

subproblems.title: A countable integer combination of oriented rectifiable pieces with finite total mass is integer multiplicity (Simon 3.8–3.9)
subproblems.statement: Assume (TL): for all P', n' ∈ ℕ, every open U' ⊆ ℝ^{P'} and all Borel A ⊆ B ⊆ U' with Hⁿ'(B ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U', for Hⁿ'-a.e. x ∈ A and every subspace Q, B has approximate tangent space Q at x iff A does. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, and for j ∈ ℕ let N_j ⊆ U be Borel and countably n-rectifiable, g_j : ℝ^P → ℤ measurable with g_j(y) ≠ 0 for y ∈ N_j, and η_j : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) strongly measurable such that for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_j, η_j(y) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of N_j at y. Assume Σ_j ∫⁻_{N_j} |g_j| dHⁿ < ∞ and let Q ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy Q(ω) = Σ_j ∫_{N_j} g_j(y)·η_j(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Then Q is integer multiplicity (IsIntegerMultiplicity Q).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → A ⊆ B → B ⊆ U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict A), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (N : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (g : ℕ → Euclid P → ℤ) (η : ℕ → Euclid P → MultiVector P n) (Q : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → (∀ j, MeasurableSet (N j)) → (∀ j, N j ⊆ U) → (∀ j, CountablyRectifiable n (N j)) → (∀ j, Measurable (g j)) → (∀ j, ∀ y ∈ N j, g j y ≠ 0) → (∀ j, StronglyMeasurable (η j)) → (∀ j, ∀ᵐ y ∂(μHE[n].restrict (N j)), ∃ T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (N j) y T ∧ IsUnitOrientationOf (η j y) T) → ∑' j, ∫⁻ y in N j, ((g j y).natAbs : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n] ≠ ∞ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Q ω = ∑' j, ∫ y in N j, (g j y : ℝ) * η j y ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y) ∂μHE[n]) → IsIntegerMultiplicity Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 8 (N and its finite measure), 9 (common tangent planes and the orientation η), 10 (the integer multiplicity k and dominated convergence) and 11 (the triple) of the parent proof, Simon 3.7–3.9; the final triple is built by the sibling imrep_of_density (accepted cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density), which takes the carrier {k ≠ 0}, multiplicity |k| and orientation sign(k)η exactly as in step 11. Siblings used: orient_algebra, imrep_of_density, int_density.
1. The union. N := ⋃_j N_j is Borel, N ⊆ U, and N is countably n-rectifiable (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.countablyRectifiable_iUnion). Since g_j is a nonzero integer on N_j, |g_j| ≥ 1 there, so Hⁿ(N) ≤ Σ_j Hⁿ(N_j) ≤ Σ_j ∫⁻_{N_j} |g_j| dHⁿ < ∞; in particular Hⁿ(N ∩ C) < ∞ for every compact C ⊆ U.
2. Tangent planes of N. Fix j. (TL) with (U, A := N_j, B := N) (N_j ⊆ N ⊆ U Borel, step 1) gives: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_j and every subspace T, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N y T ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N_j y T. With the hypothesis on η_j: (O_j) for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_j there is T with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N y T and η_j(y) a unit orientation of T. Consequently (ae_restrict_iUnion_iff, ae_all_iff, and N_i ∩ N_j ⊆ N_j): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N, (O_j) holds at y for every j with y ∈ N_j. Call such y good.
3. Common orientation. Lean instance note: PseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) is not found by instance search; provide it by haveI : TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) := @PseudoEMetricSpace.pseudoMetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) inferInstance, after which TopologicalSpace.MetrizableSpace (MultiVector P n) is inferred; avoid finite sums of MultiVector-valued functions (ContinuousAdd is not found by instance search). For y ∈ N let j₀(y) be the least j with y ∈ N_j and put η(y) := η_{j₀(y)}(y); put η(y) := 0 for y ∉ N. Strong measurability: with the disjoint Borel sets D_j := N_j ∖ ⋃_{i<j} N_i (⋃_j D_j = N) define u_0 := 0 and u_{k+1}(y) := η_k(y) if y ∈ D_k, u_{k+1}(y) := u_k(y) otherwise; each u_k is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.ite), and for each y the sequence u_k(y) is eventually equal to η(y) (from k = j₀(y) + 1 on if y ∈ N, constantly 0 otherwise), so η is strongly measurable (stronglyMeasurable_of_tendsto). For good y, (O_{j₀(y)}) says that η(y) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of N at y; so this holds for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N.
4. Signs. For j ∈ ℕ let ε_j(y) := 1 if η_j(y) = η(y) and ε_j(y) := −1 otherwise (ℤ-valued); ε_j is measurable because {η_j = η} is measurable (StronglyMeasurable.measurableSet_eq_fun, using the metrizable instance of step 3). If y is good and y ∈ N_j, then (O_j) and (O_{j₀(y)}) give approximate tangent spaces T, T' of N at y oriented by η_j(y) and η(y); by uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) T = T', so by orient_algebra (a) η_j(y) = η(y) or η_j(y) = −η(y), i.e. η_j(y) = ε_j(y)·η(y). Hence for every j, η_j = ε_j·η Hⁿ-a.e. on N_j.
5. The integer density. Let f_j := 1_{N_j}·ε_j·g_j : ℝ^P → ℤ (measurable; |f_j| = 1_{N_j}|g_j|), so Σ_j ∫⁻ |f_j| dHⁿ = Σ_j ∫⁻_{N_j} |g_j| dHⁿ < ∞. int_density gives a measurable m : ℝ^P → ℝ, integer valued at every point, with |m(y)| ≤ S(y) := Σ_j |f_j(y)| for every y and, for Hⁿ-a.e. y, (f_j(y))_j summable with m(y) = Σ_j f_j(y). Hence ∫⁻_{N∩C} |m| dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻ S dHⁿ = Σ_j ∫⁻_{N_j} |g_j| dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact C (lintegral_tsum).
6. Representation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By orient_algebra (b) and the a.e. orientation properties, |η_j(y)(ω(y))| ≤ C_ω for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_j and |η(y)(ω(y))| ≤ C_ω for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N. Then: (i) by step 4, ∫_{N_j} g_j·η_j(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{N_j} g_j·ε_j·η(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_N f_j·η(ω) dHⁿ (N_j ⊆ N, f_j = 0 off N_j); (ii) the functions f_j·η(ω) are a.e. strongly measurable on N and Σ_j ∫⁻_N |f_j·η(ω)| dHⁿ ≤ C_ω·Σ_j ∫⁻_{N_j} |g_j| dHⁿ < ∞, so integral_tsum gives Σ_j ∫_N f_j·η(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_N Σ_j f_j(y)·η(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y); (iii) for Hⁿ-a.e. y, (f_j(y)) is summable with sum m(y) (step 5), so Σ_j f_j(y)·η(y)(ω(y)) = m(y)·η(y)(ω(y)) (tsum_mul_right). With the hypothesis on Q: Q(ω) = Σ_j ∫_{N_j} g_j·η_j(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_N m(y)·η(y)(ω(y)) dHⁿ(y).
7. The triple. imrep_of_density with (U, N, η, m): U is open, N is Borel, N ⊆ U, N is countably n-rectifiable and Hⁿ(N ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (step 1), η is strongly measurable (step 3), m is measurable and integer valued (step 5), ∫⁻_{N∩K} |m| dHⁿ < ∞ (step 5), and for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N, η(y) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of N at y (step 3). It gives an IMRep R' in U with R'.action(ω) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ for every n-form ω. By step 6, Q(ω) = R'.action(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), i.e. R' represents Q. Hence IsIntegerMultiplicity Q. ∎
